canvas.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "canvas and playground container" — narrower than the prior "page/app background" meaning, now specifically the live-preview/demo container surface. Value moved off neutral.white (was briefly byte-identical to bg.surface/bg.neutral-subtle) to gray.100, one step past bg.neutral-subtle (gray.50), so it reads as a visually distinct container again. Contrast re-verified: text.primary 12.41:1, text.secondary 6.05:1 — both clear AA. text.tertiary fails here at 4.13:1 (found 2026-09-03, during an unrelated Image atom review's incidental Storybook-suite run — previously unmeasured against this token specifically) — don't place text.tertiary literal text directly on bg.canvas, matching the already-documented dark-mode failure (see that theme's own description). Byte-identical to border.neutral-subtle (also gray.100) — nothing currently pairs the two, flagged here in case a future component draws a border.neutral-subtle border directly on bg.canvas.

overlay.$description: Dimming scrim behind Dialog/Drawer/overlays (Backdrop atom). No text sits directly on it, so it isn't a WCAG contrast pairing — opacity is applied separately, compositionally, via the opacity.* scale rather than baked into this token, matching how color and opacity stay separate token categories everywhere else. Shared across all 4 themes since dimming what's behind isn't a brand-dependent decision. Reordered (2026-08-20) to sit right after bg.canvas, per explicit direction — no value change.

scrim.$description: New token (2026-08-25, CloseButton review), revised same day at explicit direction to be mode-specific rather than shared across all 4 themes — light mode keeps neutral.white unchanged; dark mode moves off white to gray.800 (see that file's own description) so the scrim doesn't read as a stark bright patch against a dark-themed app. Light grounding layer behind an icon-only control sitting over unpredictable external content (CloseButton's optional hasBackground prop) — no fixed WCAG contrast pairing is possible here, since what this composites over is arbitrary and outside this system's control by design, unlike every other bg.* / text.* pairing in this file. Opacity is applied separately, compositionally, at the component layer (CloseButton.module.css, opacity.40 — also revised down from opacity.80 the same day) rather than baked into this token, matching bg.overlay's own color/opacity separation. Positioned directly after bg.overlay — both are opacity-composited overlay-type tokens, distinct from bg.skeleton's always-opaque, brand-tinted fill.

skeleton.$description: New token (2026-08-16), added for Skeleton — bg.subtle (gray.50, since renamed to bg.neutral-subtle) was the original fill, but measured directly against bg.surface (white) it is only 1.04:1, functionally invisible for a component whose entire purpose is to read as a visible placeholder shape (found reviewing Skeleton). Not a WCAG-text-contrast failure (Skeleton is decorative/aria-hidden, exempt like disabled controls) but a real functional gap — the same class of issue Phase 16's bg.*-indicator tokens closed for Badge's dot mode: an existing token verified for one purpose (bg.neutral-subtle: hover fill, dashboard panel, neutral accent) reused for a new one (a standalone visible graphic) it was never checked against. Revised same day from gray.200 to purple.200 at explicit direction, to give the skeleton fill brand identity instead of staying neutral. purple.200 vs bg.surface = 1.36:1 — effectively identical visual weight to gray.200's own 1.35:1 (deliberately matched, not coincidental), so the visibility fix carries over unchanged; only the hue changed. Brand-specific (unlike bg.neutral's brand-agnostic precedent, since the whole point here is to carry brand identity) — see emerald-light.json for that theme's own value. Reordered (2026-08-20) to sit right after bg.overlay, per explicit direction — no value change.

surface.$description: Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "page, card, sheet and drawer background" — broadens from "card/panel surface" to cover every default content surface, not just cards. Value unchanged (white). bg.surface-raised (a separate token for "an elevated surface, paired with a shadow") was retired (2026-08-20) — it was byte-identical to this token in every theme/mode (elevation always came from the paired shadow alone, never a background difference), so keeping two names for one value added a lookup with no payoff. Every former bg.surface-raised consumer now uses this token directly.

brand.$description: Primary action fill (Button primary, focus accents); also non-text graphical status indicators (Badge's brand-tone dot mode) since bg.brand-indicator was retired into this token (2026-08-21) — see this token's own dark-file description and guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md. Light value unchanged.

brand-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.brand. Light value unchanged.

brand-subtle.$description: Moved from purple.100 to purple.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction (matching bg.info-subtle's earlier move). Dark theme moved correspondingly (purple.900 → purple.950). Real consumers re-verified: Avatar's text.link (purple.600) on purple.50 = 7.03:1 (was 6.47:1 on purple.100); ListItem's selected state (text.primary, gray.900) on purple.50 = 13.46:1 — both still comfortably pass AA.

brand-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state (a subtle-background fill darkening one step on hover, the same direction bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover already use for their own solid fills). purple.100 is brand-subtle's own value before its 2026-07-27 move to purple.50, so this reuses an already-generated scale step rather than needing a new one. text.link (purple.600) on purple.100 = 6.47:1, comfortably passes AA.

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — bg.danger, text.danger, border.danger, and icon.danger now deliberately share the same primitive step per mode (red.600 light / red.300 dark), replacing what were several narrow single-purpose tokens with one reused value per category, while staying independently-tracked tokens for future divergence. Light value unchanged (red.600, 5.10:1 vs bg.surface). This also retires bg.danger-indicator: that token existed only because bg.danger's old dark value (red.500) failed WCAG 1.4.11 outright for small standalone graphics (2.90:1 against dark bg.surface) — the new dark value (red.300, see purple-dark.json) clears it comfortably, so every former bg.danger-indicator consumer now uses this token directly. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

danger-hover.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — light value unchanged (red.700). Dark value moved from red.400 to red.200, one step lighter, following bg.danger's own dark move to red.300 (keeping the same relative hover-lightening gap). text.on-danger (red.900 as of this change) on red.200 (dark) = 10.68:1.

danger-subtle.$description: Moved from red.100 to red.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (red.900 → red.950). text.danger (red.700 at the time) on red.50 = 7.05:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.43:1 on red.100). Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated light tint, independent of text.danger's own value.

danger-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses danger-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (red.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.danger (red.700 at the time) on red.100 = 6.43:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching danger-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation.

on-danger.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.danger surface (the primary action inside a solid danger Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-danger (white light / red.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.danger: 5.10:1 light / 8.22:1 dark. The fill against bg.danger itself is 5.10:1 light / 8.22:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — bg.warning, text.warning, border.warning, and icon.warning now deliberately share the same primitive step per mode (amber.600 light / amber.300 dark), replacing what were several narrow single-purpose tokens with one reused value per category, while staying independently-tracked tokens for future divergence. Light value unchanged (amber.600, 4.78:1 vs bg.surface). This also retires bg.warning-indicator: unlike danger's own old dark value (which failed outright), bg.warning's old dark value (amber.500) already cleared the 3:1 non-text floor at 3.05:1, but only barely — the new dark value (amber.300) clears it comfortably at 5.80:1, so every former bg.warning-indicator consumer now uses this token directly. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

warning-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.warning, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-warning on amber.700 = 6.96:1, passes AA. Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — light value unchanged. Dark value moved from amber.400 to amber.200, one step lighter, following bg.warning's own dark move to amber.300 (keeping the same relative hover-lightening gap). text.on-warning (amber.900 as of this change) on amber.200 (dark) = 10.54:1.

warning-subtle.$description: Moved from amber.100 to amber.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (amber.900 → amber.950). text.warning (amber.800 at the time) on amber.50 = 9.74:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.90:1 on amber.100). Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated light tint, independent of text.warning's own value.

warning-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses warning-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (amber.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.warning (amber.800 at the time) on amber.100 = 8.90:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching warning-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation.

on-warning.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.warning surface (the primary action inside a solid warning Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-warning (white light / amber.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.warning: 4.78:1 light / 8.19:1 dark. The fill against bg.warning itself is 4.78:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

success.$description: Solid fill hosting text.on-success. green.600 (pre-OKLCH-regen step) gave neither white nor gray.950 text 4.5:1 (4.39:1 / 4.13:1) — green.700 gives white text 6.50:1 (verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4). Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — bg.success, text.success, border.success, and icon.success now deliberately share the same primitive step per mode (green.700 light / green.300 dark), replacing what were several narrow single-purpose tokens with one reused value per category, while staying independently-tracked tokens for future divergence. Light value unchanged. This also retires bg.success-indicator: unlike danger's own old dark value (which failed outright) or warning's (a thin pass), bg.success's old dark value (green.500) already had real margin at 3.28:1 — the new dark value (green.300) is a clean improvement to 6.01:1, so every former bg.success-indicator consumer now uses this token directly. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

success-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.success, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-success on green.800 = 9.56:1, passes AA. Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — light value unchanged. Dark value moved from green.400 to green.200, one step lighter, following bg.success's own dark move to green.300 (keeping the same relative hover-lightening gap). text.on-success (green.900 as of this change) on green.200 (dark) = 10.32:1.

success-subtle.$description: Moved from green.100 to green.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (green.900 → green.950). text.success (green.800 at the time) on green.50 = 9.15:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 8.42:1 on green.100). Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated light tint, independent of text.success's own value.

success-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses success-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (green.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.success (green.800 at the time) on green.100 = 8.42:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching success-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation.

on-success.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.success surface (the primary action inside a solid success Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-success (white light / green.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.success: 6.50:1 light / 8.19:1 dark. The fill against bg.success itself is 6.50:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — bg.info, text.info, border.info, and icon.info now deliberately share the same primitive step per mode (blue.600 light / blue.300 dark), replacing what were several narrow single-purpose tokens with one reused value per category, while staying independently-tracked tokens for future divergence. Light value unchanged (blue.600, 4.71:1 vs bg.surface). This also retires bg.info-indicator: bg.info's old dark value (blue.500) already had real margin at 3.09:1, not a failure — the new dark value (blue.300) is a clean improvement to 5.85:1, so every former bg.info-indicator consumer now uses this token directly. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table, including the one pairing in this pass that landed uncomfortably close to the AA floor.

info-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.info, mirroring bg.brand-hover/bg.danger-hover's one-step-darker pattern (2026-07-27). White text.on-info on blue.700 = 6.93:1, passes AA. Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — light value unchanged. Dark value moved from blue.400 to blue.200, one step lighter, following bg.info's own dark move to blue.300 (keeping the same relative hover-lightening gap). text.on-info (blue.900 as of this change) on blue.200 (dark) = 10.46:1.

info-subtle.$description: Moved from blue.100 to blue.50 (2026-07-27), one step lighter, per explicit direction. Dark theme moved correspondingly (blue.900 → blue.950, the mirror-opposite extreme) to preserve the same relative gap. text.info (blue.700 at the time) on blue.50 = 6.63:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.10:1 on blue.100). Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated light tint, independent of text.info's own value. Important consequence: text.info's own light value later moved to blue.600 (see that token's own description) — blue.600 on this token (blue.50) measures only 4.5068:1, the tightest margin found across any of the four danger/warning/success/info consolidations, just above the 4.5:1 AA floor for normal text. Flagged and accepted at explicit direction rather than special-cased; worth re-checking if this primitive scale ever gets regenerated.

info-subtle-hover.$description: New token (2026-08-15), added for Avatar's hover state — reuses info-subtle's own pre-2026-07-27 value (blue.100), same pattern as bg.brand-subtle-hover. text.info (blue.700 at the time) on blue.100 = 6.10:1, comfortably passes AA. Shared across both brand themes, matching info-subtle's own brand-independence. Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation.

on-info.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.info surface (the primary action inside a solid info Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-info (white light / blue.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.info: 4.71:1 light / 8.20:1 dark. The fill against bg.info itself is 4.71:1 light / 8.20:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

highlight.$description: New token family (2026-10-04), the general highlight and accent colour on the new yellow scale, shared across both brands and not a status tone. Light: yellow.700, the darkest step that still holds white text (white on it is 4.67:1; yellow.600, the scale's anchor, is only 3.23:1). Graphical contrast vs bg.surface 4.67:1.

highlight-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.highlight. Light yellow.800: white on it is 6.89:1.

highlight-subtle.$description: Light highlight tint, the marker behind highlighted text and the fill of a subtle highlight badge. Light yellow.50: text.highlight (yellow.800) on it is 6.64:1, and icon.highlight (yellow.600) is 3.11:1, over the 3:1 non-text floor. Sits at about 1.04:1 against bg.surface, a deliberately pale tint.

highlight-subtle-hover.$description: Hover state of bg.highlight-subtle. Light yellow.100: text.highlight (yellow.800) on it is 6.13:1. icon.highlight on it is only 2.87:1, so an icon on this fill takes text.highlight's step instead.

on-highlight.$description: Inverted fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.highlight surface, the same value as text.on-highlight, its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill. White on bg.highlight is 4.67:1.

neutral.$description: Merged with the retired bg.neutral (gray.500, offline/dot-only fill) and renamed from bg.neutral-strong (2026-08-21) — this token covers both the neutral status-dot fill (Avatar's offline indicator, Badge's neutral dot) and the solid neutral fill for hosting text (Badge/Tag's solid-neutral variant, Tooltip's chrome). Light value unchanged (gray.600, shared across all 4 themes) — gray.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.70:1 (dot use, clears 3:1), white text.on-neutral on gray.600 = 4.70:1 (text use, clears 4.5:1); a single value satisfies both cases in light mode. Dark mode needed a different fix — see this token's own dark-file description.

neutral-hover.$description: Renamed from bg.neutral-strong-hover (2026-08-21), hover state of bg.neutral (formerly bg.neutral-strong). Light value unchanged (gray.700) — white text.on-neutral on gray.700 = 6.88:1, clears 4.5:1. Dark mode needed a different fix — see this token's own dark-file description.

neutral-subtle.$description: Renamed from bg.subtle (2026-08-20), grouped with the other neutral tokens here instead of sitting up near bg.canvas/bg.surface — no value change. Usage redefined (2026-08-08) to "hover fill for tertiary/ghost controls, dashboard panel, neutral accent" — broadens from hover-fill/zebra-striping to also cover dashboard panels and general neutral accents. Value unchanged (gray.50). History: swapped with canvas 2026-07-27, when this token was defined as the barely-visible tint layered on top of white bg.surface. text.tertiary against this token measures 4.51:1 — clears the 4.5:1 AA text floor, but by a razor-thin 0.01 margin; revisit if the primitive gray scale is ever regenerated. icon.default shares text.tertiary's own primitive step, so this is also the figure for Image's own fallback icon (verified 2026-09-04, finalizing Image — see icon.default's own description).

neutral-subtle-hover.$description: Renamed from bg.subtle-hover (2026-08-20), grouped with the other neutral tokens here — no value change. Originally added 2026-08-17, found adding Tag's whole-tag clickable/selectable mode — bg.neutral-subtle's own hover step, one primitive scale step further in the same direction bg.brand-subtle-hover/etc. already use (darken in light mode, lighten in dark mode). text.secondary (Tag/Badge subtleNeutral's own paired text) on gray.100 = 6.05:1, comfortably passes AA.

on-neutral.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the fill of a control drawn on a solid bg.neutral surface (the primary action inside a solid neutral Alert), an inverted fill. Same value as text.on-neutral (white light / gray.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a fill (the same pattern as bg.brand and text.brand). The control's label is text.secondary: 6.88:1 light / 10.47:1 dark. The fill against bg.neutral itself is 4.70:1 light / 8.21:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor.

track.$description: New token (2026-08-22), added for ProgressBar's empty/unfilled track — was reusing bg.neutral-subtle, the same 'existing token reused for an unverified new purpose' bug that led to bg.skeleton (Phase 18): measured directly against bg.surface, bg.neutral-subtle is only 1.04:1 in light mode, functionally near-invisible. Given its own dedicated value at explicit user direction — first gray.200 (1.35:1), revised same session to gray.100 (1.14:1 vs bg.surface) at further explicit direction — still fails the 3:1 non-text floor WCAG 1.4.11 asks for graphical objects required to understand content, and a progress track's boundary plausibly falls under that requirement (unlike border.brand-subtle/border.code, which are purely decorative accents 1.4.11 doesn't bind the same way). Chosen anyway after being shown the compliant alternative (gray.500, 3.25:1) — a deliberate, informed exception matching the common industry convention of a very faint progress track (comparable production progress-track implementations measure similarly faint, in the ~1:1 range), though none of those are themselves verified against 3:1 either. Brand-agnostic, matching bg.neutral-subtle's own precedent. Revisit with gray.500 light / gray.400 dark (3.25:1 / 4.34:1) if this needs to actually clear 3:1 later. Reused 2026-08-23 for ProgressCircle's own identical track-invisibility bug (same root cause — bg.neutral-subtle reused for an unverified purpose — same fix, no new value decision needed). **Moved back to gray.200 (2026-09-15, at explicit direction)** — this token had since become the shared 'always-interactive control track' value too (Switch, then Slider — see ADR-0016), and once several comparable production sliders/switches were checked, gray.100's near-1:1 faintness read as too subtle for those two specifically; still a deliberate sub-3:1 exception either way (1.35:1, up from 1.14:1), not a compliance claim — see 03-token-system-spec.md's 'Notable exceptions'. Dark value (gray.800, 1.40:1) left unchanged.

track-strong.$description: New token (2026-08-30), added for Switch's unchecked-state track fill — was reusing bg.neutral-subtle, the exact 'existing token reused for an unverified new purpose' bug already fixed twice (bg.skeleton, Phase 18; bg.track, above): measured directly against bg.surface, bg.neutral-subtle is only 1.04:1 in light mode, functionally near-invisible. Unlike bg.track's own deliberate sub-3:1 exception (a passive progress indicator), Switch is an always-visible interactive control whose off state needed to read as a real UI boundary under WCAG 1.4.11 at the time — so this token used the compliant value bg.track's own description already named as the alternative: gray.500 vs bg.surface = 3.25:1, clearing the 3:1 non-text floor. Brand-agnostic, matching bg.track/bg.neutral-subtle's own precedent. **Moved to gray.300 (2026-09-15, at explicit direction)** — Switch's own *resting* unchecked state no longer consumes this token (moved to bg.track, see ADR-0016), leaving Indicators' inactive-dot fill as its resting-state consumer; measures ~1.72:1 against bg.surface — now itself a deliberate sub-3:1 exception rather than a compliant value, the same category bg.track already occupies. **Flagged, not silently applied:** Indicators' own review explicitly chose gray.500 specifically because its dot is a real, clickable control the 3:1 floor was judged to genuinely apply to (unlike a passive track) — this move reopens that same question for Indicators without a fresh review of its own; see guidelines/component-reviews/Indicators.md. **Also reused, same day, at explicit direction, for Switch's own unchecked-hover state** — replacing bg.neutral there (gray.600 light / gray.300 dark, 3.25:1/8.21:1), which had been this token's own hover-state pairing back when this token was Switch's resting color. Since Switch's resting state is now bg.track (gray.200), the hover step to this token (gray.300, one primitive step) is real and measurable via computed style (`rgb(222,221,229)` → `rgb(198,196,209)`) but visually subtle in light mode specifically — live-verified, not just computed; a noticeably smaller step than bg.neutral's own jump gave.

code.$description: New token (2026-08-08) for inline code/token-reference pills in Storybook documentation (docs.css's inline-code and token-table pill rules) — mirrors bg.info-subtle's exact blue.50/blue.950 lightness-curve values, but under a name that doesn't imply status/info meaning, since a plain code reference isn't a status. Retired 2026-08-20 in favor of bg.info-subtle directly; restored the same day, reversing that retirement — every former bg.info-subtle-standing-in-for-bg.code consumer (docs.css's two inline-code pill rules) uses this token again. Adopted by the real Code.tsx atom (2026-09-06, at explicit direction, during its own review pass) — previously that component used bg.neutral-subtle instead; the shipped atom and the Storybook-docs inline-code pill now share the identical bg.code/border.code/text.secondary treatment rather than looking like two different things.

code-highlight.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s highlighted lines. blue.100, a step deeper than `bg.code` (blue.50). Every `text.syntax-*` colour clears 4.5:1 on it (5.3:1 or more); `text.secondary`, which the line numbers use, clears it too.

code-block.$description: New token (2026-09-26), the background of `CodeBlock`. Same value as `bg.code` (blue.50) in light mode, so a block and an inline `Code` match. Every `text.syntax-*` colour and `text.secondary` (line numbers, the title) is measured against it.

tertiary.$description: gray.500 fails AA (needs 4.5:1) for this token's literal-text uses (Text color="tertiary", Divider label, Input placeholder). gray.600 gives 4.70:1 (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen), still lighter/more muted than text.secondary (gray.700).

on-brand.$description: Text/icons on a solid bg.brand fill. Light value unchanged (white) — dark mode's own value is now unified across both brand themes, see this token's own dark-file description.

on-danger.$description: Text on a solid bg.danger fill. White on red.600 = 5.10:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use red.900 instead (changed 2026-08-20 from gray.950, as part of the danger token consolidation — see purple-dark.json's own description).

on-info.$description: Text on a solid bg.info fill. White on blue.600 = 4.71:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use blue.900 instead (changed 2026-08-20 from gray.950, as part of the info token consolidation — see purple-dark.json's own description).

on-success.$description: Text on a solid bg.success fill. White on green.700 = 6.50:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use green.900 instead (changed 2026-08-20 from gray.950, as part of the success token consolidation — see purple-dark.json's own description).

on-warning.$description: Text on a solid bg.warning fill. White on amber.600 = 4.78:1, passes AA (re-verified 2026-07-18, Phase 4 OKLCH regen). Dark themes use amber.900 instead (changed 2026-08-20 from gray.950, as part of the warning token consolidation — see purple-dark.json's own description).

on-neutral.$description: Text on a solid bg.neutral fill (Badge solid variant) — renamed from bg.neutral-strong, 2026-08-21. Light value unchanged (white). White on gray.600 = 4.70:1, passes.

on-highlight.$description: Text on a solid bg.highlight fill. White on yellow.700: 4.67:1.

link.$description: Token update (2026-08-20), at explicit direction — moved off the brand anchor (was purple.600 in this theme, emerald.700 in the other) to a shared blue.600, now literally identical across both brand themes and both modes (this file and emerald-light.json both use blue.600; both dark files use blue.300). De-brands link color entirely — links no longer visually match the active brand identity, instead using a fixed, universal link-blue regardless of theme, matching the broader web convention this token's own name implies. blue.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.71:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 7.37:1 on the old purple.600 — a real margin drop, but not a near-miss). Byte-identical to text.info's own light value as a direct consequence — not a problem (separate tokens, independently tracked, just a coincidental shared step), but worth knowing. text.brand (below) is NOT changed by this — it keeps the brand-anchor value this token used to share, and its own description no longer claims equivalence with this token. Two real consumers that relied on text.link's old brand-matching behavior (Avatar's default `.content` fill, Storybook's own toolbar `colorSecondary`) were moved to text.brand instead, to preserve their existing, previously-verified appearance (see Phase 11/12 above) — every other consumer (Heading/Text/Link's own `colorLink` variants) picks up the new blue as intended.

brand.$description: Accent text drawn from the brand color (2026-07-27) — for emphasis/labels, not links. Originally reused text.link's own resolved value (both needed an AA-safe brand-colored text color on bg.surface); text.link was de-branded to a shared blue (2026-08-20, see that token's own description), so this token now stands on its own — value unchanged, still purple.600 on white = 7.37:1. NOT a literal 'primitive step 600 in every theme' constant — emerald-light/both dark themes use a different step (see emerald-light.json / *-dark.json).

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.700 to red.600, so text.danger now shares the same primitive step as bg.danger/border.danger/icon.danger in light mode. red.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 5.10:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 7.39:1). See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full rationale and contrast table.

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.800 to amber.600, so text.warning now shares the same primitive step as bg.warning/border.warning/icon.warning in light mode. amber.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.78:1, still passes AA (was 10.14:1) — a bigger margin drop than danger's own equivalent move, since amber.800 sat unusually high on the scale to begin with; still a real, deliberate pass, not a near-miss. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full rationale and contrast table.

success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.800 to green.700, so text.success now shares the same primitive step as bg.success/border.success/icon.success in light mode. green.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.50:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 9.56:1) — a much smaller margin drop than warning's own equivalent move, since green.800 was only one step off the shared target rather than two. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full rationale and contrast table.

info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.700 to blue.600, so text.info now shares the same primitive step as bg.info/border.info/icon.info in light mode. blue.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.71:1, still comfortably passes AA (was 6.93:1). Against bg.info-subtle specifically, this measures only 4.5068:1 — the tightest margin found across this whole family of consolidations; see bg.info-subtle's own description for the full note. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full rationale and contrast table.

highlight.$description: New token family (2026-10-04), the general highlight and accent colour on the new yellow scale, shared across both brands and not a status tone. Light yellow.800 as literal text: 6.89:1 vs bg.surface, 6.64:1 on bg.highlight-subtle and 6.13:1 on bg.highlight-subtle-hover. yellow.700 would be 4.67:1 on the surface but 4.50:1 on the subtle fill and only 4.16:1 on its hover, so it is not used. It is 6.06:1 on bg.canvas.

syntax-keyword.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — keywords and at-rules (`const`, `if`, `@media`). purple.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 9.4:1 — AA.

syntax-string.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — string literals. green.800 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 8.4:1 — AA.

syntax-number.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — numbers, units and the literals `true`, `false`, `null`. amber.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.1:1 — AA.

syntax-function.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — function and command names at a call. blue.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.1:1 — AA.

syntax-type.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — type and class names (`Promise`, `Button`). emerald.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 5.3:1 — AA.

syntax-property.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — object keys, CSS properties and HTML/JSX attribute names. blue.800 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 8.9:1 — AA.

syntax-tag.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — HTML/JSX tag names. red.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.5:1 — AA.

syntax-comment.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — comments — muted by hue, not by contrast, so it still clears AA. gray.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.1:1 — AA.

syntax-inserted.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — an added line in a diff. green.800 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 8.4:1 — AA.

syntax-deleted.$description: New token (2026-09-26), for `CodeBlock`'s syntax highlighting — a removed line in a diff. red.700 in this theme, shared across both brands (code colours are not brand-tinted, like `text.link`). Measured against the two backgrounds it is drawn on, `bg.code-block` and the highlighted-line band `bg.code-highlight`, and the lower ratio is 6.5:1 — AA.

white.$description: White in all 4 themes and both modes, for text drawn on a surface that is dark in every theme (the ImageViewer stage over bg.overlay). Shares the reasoning of icon.white: bg.overlay stays neutral.black in dark mode, so a text token that flipped dark would be invisible there. Not for text on a themed surface: use text.primary or text.on-* there. Like bg.overlay, no fixed WCAG pairing (what is behind the scrim is arbitrary); white on bg.overlay at opacity.80 over the whitest content is 12.6:1.

neutral-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.subtle (2026-08-21), part of a border.* identifier rotation (border.subtle→border.neutral-subtle, border.strong→border.neutral, border.neutral→border.neutral-strong, border.neutral-strong→border.strong) — no values changed anywhere in this rotation, only names; see guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md for the full rationale. Faint divider/low-emphasis border tint. Storybook-chrome only today (docs.css, Foundations block components) — no published component consumes it directly.

neutral.$description: Renamed from border.strong (2026-08-21), part of the same border.* rotation (see border.neutral-subtle's own description). This is the system's most widely consumed generic gray border — the default resting border on Checkbox/Kbd (not hover), and the hover-state border on Select/Input/Textarea/Button's secondary variant/IconButton/Indicators. Color.mdx's own usage text ('Hover-state border emphasis') predates this full consumer list and doesn't capture the non-hover cases — a pre-existing documentation gap noted here, not something this rename introduces or fixes. Blockquote moved off this token onto border.brand instead (2026-09-06, at explicit direction, during its own review pass) — see that token's own description.

neutral-strong.$description: Renamed from border.neutral (2026-08-21), part of a border.* identifier rotation (border.subtle→border.neutral-subtle, border.strong→border.neutral, border.neutral→border.neutral-strong, border.neutral-strong→border.strong) — no values changed anywhere in this rotation, only names; see guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md for the full rationale. Originally added (2026-08-20) to complete the border.danger/warning/success/info/brand state-identifying family for the neutral tone — the token now named border.neutral (gray.400), the only existing generic gray border at the time, was measured rather than assumed and fails outright as a real state-identifying border (2.32:1 against bg.surface, under the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor; that token is documented as hover-state/default border emphasis, not state-identification). gray.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.70:1, a comfortable margin. First consumed 2026-08-23 by Checkbox's unchecked `:hover` state (previously misused border.focus, which is meant for focus rings only) — Tag's outline variant still uses the token now named border.strong (gray.700, formerly this token's own sibling border.neutral-strong) for its own default border instead.

on-neutral.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.neutral surface (the secondary action inside a solid neutral Alert). Same value as text.on-neutral (white light / gray.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.neutral: 4.70:1 light / 8.21:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

strong.$description: Renamed from border.neutral-strong (2026-08-21), part of the same border.* rotation (see border.neutral-subtle's own description). Originally added (2026-08-19), found adding Tag's selectable solid-variant ring — needed a neutral border richer than the token now named border.neutral (gray.400) to read clearly as an offset-halo accent against bg.surface. Reuses the same primitive step text.secondary already uses (gray.700), but as its own independently-tracked border token rather than reusing text.secondary directly — border.* and text.* are separate categories specifically so they can diverge later without side effects on each other. gray.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.88:1. Now consumed directly by Tag's outline/selected-solid-neutral rings (Tag.module.css).

brand.$description: New token (2026-08-20) — a general-purpose default brand-colored border, for future use wherever a real (not purely decorative) brand-accent border is needed. First real consumer: Button's `secondary` variant (2026-08-23), which also adopts text.brand/icon.brand for its label/icon and switches its default fill to transparent — see that component's own review notes. Reuses bg.brand's own light-mode step (purple.600) rather than border.focus's (purple.500), giving it its own distinct identity from the focus ring. purple.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 7.37:1, clears WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor comfortably — verified as a real border pairing, not assumed from bg.brand's own (different) text-hosting contrast case. Light value unchanged. Second consumer: Blockquote's default-variant accent border (2026-09-06, at explicit direction, moved off border.neutral — see that token's own description), pairing it with the same brand family already used by Blockquote's pull-quote decorative quote mark (text.brand).

brand-subtle.$description: Renamed from border.brand (2026-08-20), for naming consistency with its sibling family tokens (border.danger-subtle/warning-subtle/success-subtle/info-subtle all carry the -subtle suffix for the same decorative-only role; this one hadn't, despite being the exact same kind of token). Value unchanged. Brand-accent border, decorative-only (2026-07-27, revised from purple.500). purple.100 on white is only 1.14:1, well below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor — deliberately accepted, since this token is for decorative UI accents rather than a border that identifies a component/state boundary (which is what 1.4.11 actually governs; border.focus/border.danger remain contrast-verified since those ARE state-identifying). No longer literal across every theme as of 2026-08-16 — dark mode moved to purple.900 (see that file's own description) so each mode gets its own similarly-subtle contrast ratio instead of sharing one literal value that read very differently against each mode's background.

danger.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from red.500 to red.600, so border.danger now shares the same primitive step as bg.danger/text.danger/icon.danger in light mode, and absorbs border.danger-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer, e.g. Tag's outline-danger border and solid-danger selected-ring accent, now uses this token directly). red.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 5.10:1, an improvement over the previous 3.48:1. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

danger-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same family.100-light/family.900-dark scale step as border.brand-subtle — not a reuse of border.danger (red.600, the stronger state-identifying border used for e.g. Input validation, where WCAG 1.4.11 actually applies). Pairs with bg.danger-subtle (red.50) for any component drawing a subtle danger-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component — first used by Avatar's `colorful` danger variant (2026-08-16), but not scoped to it. red.100 on red.50 is 1.10:1, intentionally as subtle as border.brand-subtle's 1.09:1 purple pairing. Brand-agnostic — identical value in every brand theme, same as bg.danger-subtle. Not part of the 2026-08-20 danger token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-danger.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.danger surface (the secondary action inside a solid danger Alert). Same value as text.on-danger (white light / red.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.danger: 5.10:1 light / 8.22:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

warning.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from amber.500 to amber.600, so border.warning now shares the same primitive step as bg.warning/text.warning/icon.warning in light mode, and absorbs border.warning-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer, e.g. Tag's outline-warning border and solid-warning selected-ring accent, now uses this token directly). amber.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.78:1, an improvement over the previous 3.31:1. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

warning-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.warning-subtle (amber.50) for any component's warning-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. amber.100 on amber.50 is 1.09:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 warning token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-warning.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.warning surface (the secondary action inside a solid warning Alert). Same value as text.on-warning (white light / amber.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.warning: 4.78:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

success.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from green.500 to green.700, so border.success now shares the same primitive step as bg.success/text.success/icon.success in light mode, and absorbs border.success-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer, e.g. Tag's outline-success border and solid-success selected-ring accent, now uses this token directly). green.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.50:1, an improvement over the previous 3.07:1. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

success-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.success-subtle (green.50) for any component's success-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. green.100 on green.50 is 1.09:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 success token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-success.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.success surface (the secondary action inside a solid success Alert). Same value as text.on-success (white light / green.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.success: 6.50:1 light / 8.19:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

info.$description: Token consolidation (2026-08-20) — moved from blue.500 to blue.600, so border.info now shares the same primitive step as bg.info/text.info/icon.info in light mode, and absorbs border.info-strong's former role (that token is retired — every former consumer, e.g. Tag's outline-info border and solid-info selected-ring accent, now uses this token directly). blue.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.71:1, an improvement over the previous 3.26:1. See guidelines/03-token-system-spec.md's token-consolidation phase for the full contrast table.

info-subtle.$description: Family-matched decorative-accent border, same rationale as border.danger-subtle above — pairs with bg.info-subtle (blue.50) for any component's info-tinted ring, not limited to one specific component. blue.100 on blue.50 is 1.09:1. Brand-agnostic. Not part of the 2026-08-20 info token consolidation — this tier stays its own dedicated decorative step.

on-info.$description: New token (2026-09-24), added for Alert's actions: the outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.info surface (the secondary action inside a solid info Alert). Same value as text.on-info (white light / blue.900 dark), but its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border. Against bg.info: 4.71:1 light / 8.20:1 dark, above the 3:1 non-text floor (WCAG 1.4.11).

highlight.$description: State-identifying highlight border. Light yellow.600, the scale's anchor: 3.23:1 vs bg.surface, which clears the 3:1 non-text floor with little to spare; 2.84:1 on bg.canvas, so not for a boundary on the canvas.

highlight-subtle.$description: Decorative highlight-tinted ring, around bg.highlight-subtle. Light yellow.100, the same step as bg.highlight-subtle-hover, as the other tones' subtle borders match their hover fills, about 1.1:1 against bg.surface, a deliberate exception like the other subtle borders.

on-highlight.$description: Outline of a control drawn on a solid bg.highlight surface, the same value as text.on-highlight, its own token so a component never uses a text token as a border.

code.$description: Paired with bg.code (2026-08-08) — blue.100/blue.900, a purely decorative border, not one that identifies a component/state boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor doesn't apply — same accepted class as border.brand-subtle. Briefly paired with bg.info-subtle instead (2026-08-20, when bg.code was retired) and measured 2.63:1 dark against that fill; bg.code was restored the same day, reversing that retirement, so this token is back to pairing with bg.code and its own flat gray.700 dark value — 1.09:1 light / 1.00:1 dark (byte-identical to bg.code's own dark value, an intentional flat/borderless look in that mode), an accepted tradeoff, not an oversight. Adopted by the real Code.tsx atom alongside bg.code (2026-09-06, at explicit direction) — see that token's own description.

white.$description: White in all 4 themes and both modes, for a border or focus ring drawn on a surface that is dark in every theme (the ImageViewer stage's focus ring and current-thumbnail border). Shares the reasoning of icon.white and text.white. Not for a border on a themed surface: use border.default, border.focus or the border.on-* family there.

default.$description: Mapped to gray.700 (2026-10-18, at explicit direction; was gray.600), the same step as text.secondary, so a default icon and secondary text read at one strength, and no longer the step text.tertiary shares. Verified vs bg.surface: 6.88:1; vs bg.neutral-subtle: 6.59:1; vs bg.neutral-subtle-hover and bg.canvas: 6.05:1 — all clear the 3:1 non-text floor, and the 4.5:1 text one, comfortably. Also Image's fallback icon, its default state.

secondary.$description: gray.400 on bg.surface was 2.32:1, failing the WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor (3:1) — found during the Phase 4 icon-contrast sweep (2026-07-18) while this token was still unused by any shipped component. gray.500 gives 3.25:1, and stays more muted than icon.default (gray.600, 4.70:1).

on-brand.$description: New token (2026-08-22), completing the icon and icon.on- pattern for brand (danger/warning/success/info already had both) — same value as text.on-brand (white light / gray.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.brand fill. White on bg.brand's own light value (purple.600/emerald.700) = 7.37:1/6.08:1.

danger.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the danger token consolidation — shares the same primitive step as bg.danger/text.danger/border.danger (red.600 light / red.300 dark) rather than a distinct icon-specific value. Standalone danger-tone icon, not one sitting on a solid bg.danger fill (see icon.on-danger for that case). red.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 5.10:1.

on-danger.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the danger token consolidation — same value as text.on-danger (white light / red.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.danger fill (e.g. inside a danger Button/IconButton). White on red.600 = 5.10:1.

warning.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the warning token consolidation — shares the same primitive step as bg.warning/text.warning/border.warning (amber.600 light / amber.300 dark) rather than a distinct icon-specific value. Standalone warning-tone icon, not one sitting on a solid bg.warning fill (see icon.on-warning for that case). amber.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.78:1.

on-warning.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the warning token consolidation — same value as text.on-warning (white light / amber.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.warning fill. White on amber.600 = 4.78:1.

success.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the success token consolidation — shares the same primitive step as bg.success/text.success/border.success (green.700 light / green.300 dark) rather than a distinct icon-specific value. Standalone success-tone icon, not one sitting on a solid bg.success fill (see icon.on-success for that case). green.700 vs bg.surface (white) = 6.50:1.

on-success.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the success token consolidation — same value as text.on-success (white light / green.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.success fill. White on green.700 = 6.50:1.

info.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the info token consolidation — shares the same primitive step as bg.info/text.info/border.info (blue.600 light / blue.300 dark) rather than a distinct icon-specific value. Standalone info-tone icon, not one sitting on a solid bg.info fill (see icon.on-info for that case). blue.600 vs bg.surface (white) = 4.71:1.

on-info.$description: New token (2026-08-20), added as part of the info token consolidation — same value as text.on-info (white light / blue.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.info fill. White on blue.600 = 4.71:1.

highlight.$description: Standalone highlight-tone icon. Light yellow.600, the scale's anchor: 3.23:1 vs bg.surface (non-text floor 3:1), 3.09:1 on bg.neutral-subtle, 3.11:1 on bg.highlight-subtle, but 2.84:1 on bg.canvas and 2.87:1 on bg.highlight-subtle-hover, where text.highlight's step should be used instead.

on-highlight.$description: Icon on a solid bg.highlight fill, the same value as text.on-highlight.

on-neutral.$description: New token (2026-08-22), added so Tag's solid-neutral/selected-outline-neutral icons no longer inherit color from text.on-neutral (a text token, not an icon one) — same value as text.on-neutral (white light / gray.900 dark), for an icon sitting on a solid bg.neutral fill. White on bg.neutral's own light value (gray.600) = 4.70:1.

white.$description: Renamed from icon.on-overlay (2026-09-05, at explicit direction) — a deliberate exception to this system's usual semantic-over-primitive token naming, since the value is white in all 4 themes and isn't expected to change. Original purpose unchanged: found reviewing Backdrop's own 'content on the scrim' feature (its With-content story's Spinner had no tone set, silently inheriting the browser's default black text color, functionally invisible against the dimming scrim). For an icon/spinner sitting directly on bg.overlay, distinct from every other icon.on-* token: those pair with a bg.* that gets lighter in dark mode (so the on- token flips to a dark color to match), but bg.overlay is neutral.black in all 4 themes (brand/mode-agnostic, see that token's own description) — a token that also flipped dark in dark mode would go dark-on-black, invisible. Shared across all 4 themes for the same reason bg.overlay itself is. White on bg.overlay at its default opacity.60 = 21:1 (max possible); like bg.overlay itself, not a fixed WCAG pairing at every opacity/background combination, since what's behind the scrim is arbitrary by design.
